candidate.educational_objective: Apply current authoritative guidance to identify the uniquely safest or most accurate nursing response for the clinical construct tested by V2-Q0175.

options.A: Electing hospice ends Medicare coverage for treatment of both the terminal illness and unrelated conditions because all medical care becomes the hospice's responsibility.
options.B: Hospice focuses care for the terminal illness on palliation; the election waives Medicare payment for specified terminal-illness-related services outside the hospice arrangement, while unrelated care is not automatically excluded.
options.C: The hospice election guarantees separate Medicare payment for ongoing curative treatment of the terminal illness in addition to the hospice benefit.
options.D: A beneficiary must stop disease-directed treatment for every coexisting condition before hospice services for the terminal illness can begin.

candidate.rationale: Under 42 CFR §418.24, electing Medicare hospice reflects a palliative rather than curative approach to the terminal illness and waives Medicare payment for specified services related to that terminal illness outside the hospice arrangement. The election does not automatically eliminate coverage for care unrelated to the terminal illness.
